title: Daniel Bible Quiz - Chapter 6
description: Ten questions on Daniel 6: the decree of Darius, Daniel praying at his open windows, the den of lions, and the king's decree afterward.

questions.text: How many local governors did Darius set over the kingdom?
questions.explanation: It pleased Darius to set one hundred twenty local governors over the kingdom, and over them three presidents, of whom Daniel was one.

answers.text: Three hundred
Twelve hundred
One hundred twenty
A thousand

questions.text: Why was Daniel distinguished above the presidents and the local governors?
questions.explanation: This Daniel was distinguished above them because an excellent spirit was in him, and the king thought to set him over the whole realm.

answers.text: Because an excellent spirit was in him
Because he was the oldest of the presidents
Because he was a relative of the king
Because he had paid the king much gold

questions.text: In what area did the men decide they could find an accusation against Daniel?
questions.explanation: They could find no fault in him, and said they would not find any occasion against Daniel unless they found it concerning the law of his God.

answers.text: Concerning the king's taxes
Concerning his dealings with the local governors
Concerning his food and drink
Concerning the law of his God

questions.text: What did the royal statute they proposed forbid?
questions.explanation: They proposed a decree that whoever asks a petition of any god or man for thirty days, except of the king, should be cast into the den of lions.

answers.text: Working in the palace for thirty days
Asking a petition of any god or man except the king, for thirty days
Bowing to any image except the king's image
Speaking anything evil against the king's god

questions.text: What did Daniel do when he knew the writing was signed?
questions.explanation: He went into his house, where his windows were open toward Jerusalem, and kneeled on his knees three times a day, praying and giving thanks before his God as he did before.

answers.text: He kneeled and prayed three times a day, as he did before
He hid the writing from the king
He went to the king to ask for the decree to be changed
He stopped praying until the thirty days were past

questions.text: How did the king react when he heard the accusation against Daniel?
questions.explanation: The king was very displeased, set his heart on Daniel to deliver him, and labored until the going down of the sun to rescue him.

answers.text: He was glad and signed a second decree
He ordered the accusers to be slain at once
He was very displeased and labored until sunset to rescue him
He said nothing and went back to his palace

questions.text: What was done to the mouth of the den after Daniel was cast in?
questions.explanation: A stone was brought and laid on the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet and with the signet of his lords, so that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.

answers.text: It was closed with a band of iron and bronze
A stone was laid on it and sealed with the king's own signet
It was covered with the king's own purple robe
It was left open and guarded by mighty men

questions.text: How did the king spend that night?
questions.explanation: The king went to his palace and passed the night fasting; no musical instruments were brought before him, and his sleep fled from him.

answers.text: Feasting with his lords until morning
Praying with the presidents in the palace
Sitting beside the den of lions all night
Fasting, without music, and unable to sleep

questions.text: What did Daniel say had happened in the den?
questions.explanation: Daniel said that his God had sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths, so that they had not hurt him.

answers.text: The lions had been taken out of the den
The lions had already been fed that evening
God had sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths
A man clothed in linen had carried him up

questions.text: What happened to the men who had accused Daniel?
questions.explanation: The king commanded that those men who had accused Daniel be cast into the den of lions, with their children and their wives, and the lions mauled them and broke all their bones in pieces.

answers.text: They were cast into the den of lions and mauled
They were sent away from the kingdom
They were made presidents in Daniel's place
They were cast into a burning fiery furnace
